title: Microsoft Teams: admin list of custom apps that need updates for private and shared channels
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says Microsoft Learn does not describe the compatibility list and that it is documented only in the roadmap and Message Center notice. The Teams admin release notes confirm the list; the narrower gaps about its layout, detection criteria, default and automation remain unfilled. The roadmap facts, manifest guidance, licensing and Allow or Block controls are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft's developer page says most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.
claims.quote: Most apps can support shared and private channels with a simple manifest update.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Manifest v1.25 and later use supportsChannelFeatures instead of supportedChannelTypes.
claims.quote: Replace `supportedChannelTypes` with `supportsChannelFeatures` when you update your app manifest to v1.25 or later.

claims.claim: Apps with none of the four documented dependencies on membership, Teams or SharePoint files, cross-channel data or user-type customization need only supportsChannelFeatures: tier1 and verification and testing across channels.
claims.quote: If your app doesn’t: ... Access or manage files stored in Teams or SharePoint ... Then, you only need to: 1. Add `supportsChannelFeatures`: `tier1` to your app manifest 2. Verify expected behavior, and test your app across channels

claims.claim: A v1.25-or-later manifest declaring supportedChannelTypes cannot be uploaded or submitted.
claims.quote: In app manifest v1.25 and later, use `supportsChannelFeatures` instead of `supportedChannelTypes`. If your app manifest declares `supportedChannelTypes`, you can't upload or submit your app.

claims.claim: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.
claims.quote: Apps already published with an earlier app manifest version continue to work.

claims.claim: Custom apps are developed within the organisation or commissioned from outside developers.
claims.quote: Your organization can commission the creation of custom apps for your org-specific requirements. Custom apps can be developed within your organization or by app developers outside the organization.
